summary.headline: IFB Industries Q1 FY27 revenue rose 16.65% to INR 1,529 crore and PAT to INR 38.06 crore, but commodity and forex costs were not passed on.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 16.65% YoY to INR 1,529 crore, with PBDIT up 26.46% to INR 88.46 crore (5.79% margin vs 5.34%). PAT rose to INR 38.06 crore (2.5% of revenue) from INR 25.36 crore. Management said commodity and forex pressures are not behind it and that price increases taken so far do not cover them. Cost initiatives (about INR 42-43 crore in Q1) and a gross margin down about 160 bps cushioned the P&L. Home Appliances (HAD) revenue grew 18%, and Engineering grew 17% with EBITDA in line with budget. The Steel division posted a loss in the quarter, and the Motor division was not discussed on the call.

segments.name: Home Appliances (HAD)
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 18% in Q1; management cited 14% volume growth for IFB Industries. Front-load volume grew 9-10%, top-load over 20%, and AC 6-8%. Management said July was also good.

segments.name: Room AC
segments.commentary: Growth was about 6-8% in volume versus an industry growth rate the analyst put at 20%+. Old-rating stock was cleared by January, and the new-rating models are about 10-15% pricier than the market. Capacity is about 75,000 units/month, with peak use at 85%.

segments.name: Engineering
segments.commentary: Sales grew 17% and exceeded budget, with EBITDA in line with budget. Management targets around 20% growth and a long-term INR 2,000 crore top line, with INR 250 crore+ of OEM business in closing.

segments.name: Steel
segments.commentary: The quarter was loss-making because steel prices rose about INR 4,125 per tonne in the quarter. Management expects price pass-through from the next quarter, and says ROCE is about 20%.

segments.name: Services (HAD)
segments.commentary: Services revenue grew about 17% in the last quarter discussed. Management said the business is double-digit PBT margin, but gave no number.

segments.name: IFB Refrigeration (associate, 41.40% stake)
segments.commentary: Share of profit was INR 0.33 crore (INR 33 lakh) on PBT of INR 80 lakh. Management declined to discuss the company's performance; the call contained conflicting references to 14% (IFB Industries branches) vs 2% (company) sales growth.

guidance_outlook: HAD revenue growth of about 20% targeted; Q1 delivered 18% and management said it is 'on the right path'.
Cost initiatives of INR 120-150 crore targeted for FY27, after about INR 42-43 crore in Q1 and INR 67 crore in FY26.
Commodity and forex headwinds expected to continue; management does not see them behind the company yet.
Long-term PBDIT target stated as 'early double digit' for Home Appliances.
Engineering expects growth similar to Q1 (around 20%) and a path to INR 2,000 crore+ top line, dependent on the Tata battery project and other OEM business.
AC market share aspiration of 7-10%, with no timeline given.
Full-year capex of about INR 110 crore; Stamping capex of about INR 400 crore tied to around INR 1,000 crore of business.
capex_capacity: RAC capacity is about 75,000 units/month, with peak utilisation at 85%; debottlenecking and automation can lift output to 75,000-80,000 with no added shifts.
Management said no capacity augmentation is needed for Home Appliances at present; products for currently unserved capacities are expected within 3-6 months.
Engineering: land acquired in Gujarat for an EV battery project and stamping. Stamping capacity expansion planned in Gujarat, Gurgaon and Bangalore, with capex of about INR 400 crore.
Tata battery project (LOI about INR 150 crore) is under review after Tata Sons' decision; capex on machinery has not started. Full-year capex is about INR 110 crore.
demand_pricing: Commodity and forex costs were not passed on to customers; price increases were taken across all categories but are not enough to offset them. Some were led even where the market had not followed.
The gross margin fell about 160 bps on material costs, while absolute gross profit rose on revenue growth.
Management said some of its competitors are not raising prices either, and said it will not match them if that leaves it at a disadvantage.
SKU rationalisation cut front-load models from 55-57 to 24-25 and washer SKUs from about 9,500 to about half.
Trade schemes and discounts were about INR 1,800 crore per the analyst. Management said it would review the spend for leakages but did not confirm the figure.
Engineering business pipeline: INR 250 crore+ of OEM business close to closing.

qa_highlights.question: Has the commodity and forex pressure eased, and how much has been passed on?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said commodity and forex are not behind the company. Price increases have not offset the costs; cost savings have partly absorbed the impact.

qa_highlights.question: Why did RAC grow only about 10% when the industry grew 20%+?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it chose not to carry older-rated AC stock, which was cleared by January. The new-rated models are about 10-15% pricier, and it is focusing on higher-capacity models.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Q1 growth rate hold for the rest of the year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it expects around 20% growth; Q1 delivered 18% and July was also good. It cited improved counter placements and in-store promoters.

qa_highlights.question: What are the cost reduction targets and how much has been achieved?
qa_highlights.answer: Target is INR 120-150 crore for FY27 (earlier INR 150 crore), with about INR 42-43 crore achieved in Q1 and INR 67 crore in FY26. No counters or manning cuts are planned.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Engineering growth plan and battery project status?
qa_highlights.answer: The Tata battery LOI of about INR 150 crore is on hold after Tata Sons' decision. Management is holding the land and continuing talks; other OEM business (INR 250 crore+) is in close pipeline.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Steel make a loss, and when will it recover?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said steel prices rose about INR 4,125/tonne in the quarter. It expects pass-through to customers in coming quarters; ROCE is about 20%.

risks_watch: Commodity and forex headwinds without matching price pass-through; gross margin down about 160 bps YoY.
AC growth lagging the industry, and the new BEE rating moving AC models into a higher price band.
Tata battery project uncertainty, which affects Engineering's INR 2,000 crore target and stamping capex.
Steel loss-making in Q1; recovery depends on price pass-through.
Related-party disclosure gap: management declined to discuss IFB Refrigeration and Motor division, and the 14% vs 2% growth gap is unexplained.
Engineering Fine Blanking Q1 FY26 revenue figure changed from INR 186 crore to INR 176 crore; management to revert.
summary.management_tone: Confident on top-line momentum (18% HAD growth, Engineering ahead of budget) but cautious on margins, with commodity and forex stated as unresolved. Evasive on the associate (IFB Refrigeration), Motor division and market share data, deferring or declining several questions.
key_quotes: And whether it is behind us, as of now, no. So we are still seeing commodity increases that are there, as well as Forex.
We have taken price increases in the last quarter across all our categories. It is not enough to cover the commodity and ForEx, but wherever there's an opportunity, we have been able to take that.
So PBDIT should be early double digit in my opinion.
We are definitely on track as far as the INR150 crores cost initiatives are concerned.

financial_highlights.change: ahead of budget; EBITDA as budgeted
FY26 full year was about INR 67 crore

adds.what: RAC debottlenecking and automation lifting output to 75,000-80,000 units/month with no added shifts
Stamping capacity expansion in Gujarat, Gurgaon and Bangalore

growth.why: Management targets about 20% HAD revenue growth (Q1 at 18%) and INR 120-150 crore of FY27 cost initiatives after INR 42-43 crore in Q1, but commodity and forex costs are not passed on and the brief shows no specific orders or new capacity behind the HAD target beyond RAC debottlenecking to 75-80k units/month and stamping capex of about INR 400 crore.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Gross margin fell about 160 bps and price hikes do not cover commodity/forex, but FY27 cost initiatives of INR 120-150 crore (INR 42-43 crore in Q1) and Steel price pass-through from next quarter could lift PBDIT, which rose to 5.79% from 5.34%.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: RAC debottlenecking and automation lift output from 75,000 to 75,000-80,000 units/month (about 6.7%) with peak use at 85%, planned within the window, while stamping capex of about INR 400 crore is approved but has no commissioning date.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management guides about 20% HAD revenue growth against 18% in Q1, with July described as good and 14% HAD volume growth cited; RAC volume grew only 6-8% against an industry above 20%.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: RAC peak utilisation is 85%, but management says no capacity augmentation is needed for Home Appliances and full-year capex is only about INR 110 crore, so a new announcement is conditional on Stamping and Engineering progress.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: HAD growth is 18% against a 20% aspiration and commodity/forex costs are unresolved, so there is no sign of raising guidance.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Commodity and forex headwinds continue without full pass-through (gross margin down about 160 bps), Tata battery LOI of INR 150 crore is on hold, and Steel was loss-making in Q1.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Management said products for currently unserved capacities are expected within 3-6 months, and new-rated RAC models are being launched at 10-15% higher prices.

rows.label: Engineering OEM business INR 250 crore+ closing
rows.why: INR 250 crore+ of OEM business is described as close to closing, supporting Engineering growth of about 20% against an INR 2,000 crore long-term top line.

rows.label: Steel price pass-through and recovery
rows.why: Steel was loss-making after prices rose about INR 4,125/tonne, and management expects pass-through from the next quarter with ROCE about 20%.

rows.label: FY27 cost initiatives INR 120-150 crore
rows.why: About INR 42-43 crore was achieved in Q1 against INR 67 crore for all of FY26, so the INR 120-150 crore target implies roughly INR 80-110 crore over the remaining three quarters.

tone.note: Management was confident on 18% HAD growth, Engineering ahead of budget and cost initiatives, but cautious on commodity/forex pass-through and evasive on IFB Refrigeration, Motor and market share; analysts pushed on RAC lagging the 20%+ industry, the 14% vs 2% growth gap and trade spend.
